propositions: Path.rglob traversal on tmp_path catches PermissionError but not FileNotFoundError when a cached child directory disappears mid-walk, causing fixture teardown to fail on Python 3.11 while Python 3.12+ walk semantics tolerate the same concurrent mutation

_remove_readonly_run_snapshots fixture descends into live tracker lock directories that are intentionally created and removed by canonical LockHandle.release(), creating a race where the lock vanishes between parent scandir and child descent

Ambient Path() factory calls in teardown code select WindowsPath on Python 3.11 when os.name is monkeypatched by concurrent tests, raising NotImplementedError before cleanup completes, even though the underlying dirpath string and os.walk behavior are correct

Recursive exact-root cleanup must preserve FileNotFoundError tolerance for concurrently vanishing entries while re-raising all other walk errors and maintaining arbitrary-depth .rebar/run_snapshots discovery

os.walk with onerror callback and type-stable path construction are required to handle both the disappearing lock directory and shared os.name monkeypatch without weakening non-disappearance error detection or breaking adjacent snapshot preservation
